title: Subspace topology
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and $Y\subseteq X$ a subset. The *subspace topology* (induced topology) on $Y$ is the topology whose open sets are the sets $V\cap Y$ with $V$ open in $X$, i.e. the coarsest topology making the inclusion $Y\to X$ continuous.

source.place: Definition 5.10.1, tag 0055 (definition-Krull), item (4): $\dim(U)$ for an open $U\subset X$ is the Krull dimension of $U$ as a topological space with the induced topology (convention of Section 5.1 of topology.tex)
